notes.reason: The words are Liron's own, spoken as the guest on Milk Road AI and republished on his Substack: "If you naively extrapolate Anthropic's valuation or revenue for another couple years — 'cause they're growing, what is it, 50x per year? So a couple more 50xs and you're talking real money." The trouble is that the note's correction is a different measurement, not a refutation. The note measures year over year (CNBC: $65 billion run rate in July 2026, "a sevenfold increase from a year ago") and calendar 2025 (about $1 billion to $9 billion). Liron is extrapolating the current pace, and on that reading his figure is defensible: the run rate went from $9 billion at the end of 2025 to $47 billion in May 2026 (TechCrunch), which annualises to roughly 50x, and Anthropic's own CEO said in May 2026 "We tried to plan very well for a world of 10x growth per year. And yet we saw 80x", describing annualised growth in the first quarter of 2026 (VentureBeat, New York Times). So a note saying "7-10x per year, not 50x" contradicts Dario Amodei's own stated number, and Liron would answer with that quote in one line. He also flagged the figure as a guess ("what is it, 50x per year?"). The sources say what the note quotes, but the correction rests on choosing the year-over-year convention over the annualised one, which is a framing difference, not an error in the post.
